pharm: Oral third-generation cephalosporin prodrug (cefditoren pivoxil) hydrolyzed to active cefditoren; bactericidal beta-lactam.
quick: 200-400 mg twice daily depending on indication
Take with food to improve absorption
Use only if clearly needed (former category B)
summary: Cefditoren pivoxil (Spectracef) is an oral third-generation cephalosporin prodrug used for mild-to-moderate respiratory and skin infections. Absorption is enhanced by food, and it should not be used for long-term therapy because the pivoxil ester depletes carnitine. It is contraindicated in carnitine deficiency, milk-protein hypersensitivity (formulation contains sodium caseinate), and serious cephalosporin/penicillin allergy. Dose reduction is needed in moderate-to-severe renal impairment.
indications: Acute bacterial exacerbation of chronic bronchitis
admin: Take with meals to enhance absorption
Do not use for prolonged therapy (pivoxil-induced carnitine depletion)
Avoid with antacids and H2-blockers, which reduce absorption (acidic environment needed)
Reduce dose in moderate-to-severe renal impairment
moa: Bactericidal beta-lactam; cefditoren binds penicillin-binding proteins and inhibits bacterial cell wall (peptidoglycan) synthesis, leading to cell lysis. It is stable against many common beta-lactamases.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to cefditoren or other cephalosporins
Carnitine deficiency or conditions causing carnitine deficiency
Milk protein hypersensitivity (formulation contains sodium caseinate, not lactose intolerance)
monitor: Signs of C. difficile colitis with prolonged/repeated use

preg: Use only if clearly needed; cephalosporins generally considered low risk (former category B), but adequate human data are limited.
lact: Limited data; cephalosporins are generally excreted in low amounts in milk; use with caution.
renal: Reduce dose in moderate-to-severe renal impairment (max 200 mg BID for CrCl 30-49; 200 mg once daily for CrCl <30). Not recommended with end-stage renal disease without adequate data.
hepatic: No dose adjustment needed for mild-to-moderate hepatic impairment; not studied in severe impairment.

major: Antacids and H2-receptor antagonists - significantly reduce cefditoren absorption (avoid concurrent use)
moderate: Probenecid - increases cefditoren plasma levels (reduced renal clearance)
minor: Other carnitine-depleting agents (e.g., valproate) - additive carnitine loss
interactions.food: Take with food to enhance absorption
interactions.diagnostics: May cause false-positive urine glucose with copper-reduction tests and false-positive direct Coombs test.

monitoring: Avoid prolonged courses (carnitine status if long-term)
counsel: Take with food and complete the full prescribed course
Do not take antacids or acid-reducing medicines at the same time
Tell your doctor if you are allergic to penicillins or cephalosporins, or have a milk-protein allergy
Report rash, severe or bloody diarrhea, or difficulty breathing
This is intended for short courses only
pk: Room temperature 20-25 C; protect from moisture
pearls: Source: US Spectracef (cefditoren pivoxil) prescribing information and standard references; this label was not retrievable via openFDA at time of authoring
Pivoxil prodrug depletes carnitine - avoid long-term use and contraindicated in carnitine deficiency
Formulation contains sodium caseinate - contraindicated in milk-protein hypersensitivity (not the same as lactose intolerance)
Absorption is acid- and food-dependent - avoid antacids/H2-blockers and take with meals
Good activity against respiratory pathogens including beta-lactamase producers
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered with food; if it is nearly time for the next dose, skip it. Do not double the dose. Complete the full course.
overdose: Limited data; overdose may cause GI upset (nausea, vomiting, diarrhea) and, with renal impairment, neurotoxicity/seizures. Provide supportive care; hemodialysis can remove cefditoren if needed in severe overdose with renal failure.
